examples.ko: 할아버지가 들려주시는 영웅담은 언제 들어도 재미있어요.
examples.en: Grandfather's hero stories are fun no matter when I hear them.
The children's eyes sparkled as they listened to the hero story.

examples.ko: 모임에서 자기 영웅담만 늘어놓는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone at the gathering who only keeps going on about his own heroic tales.
They say this hero story is passed down in many countries.

examples.ko: 그 책은 평범한 사람들의 영웅담을 모았어요.
examples.en: That book collects hero stories of ordinary people.
I want to become brave like the protagonist of a hero story.

explain: 영웅의 이야기를 뜻하지만, 일상에서는 자기가 한 대단한 일을 자랑하듯 말하는 이야기에도 '영웅담을 늘어놓다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '무용담'이 있는데, 용감하게 싸우거나 모험한 이야기에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: My uncle went on again with his army hero stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 한 대단한 일을 자랑하듯 길게 이야기하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes boasting at length about one's great deeds.

phrases.en: I listened to my grandfather's war stories of bravery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸우거나 모험한 이야기에 더 잘 어울리는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that fits stories of fighting or adventure better.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 이 마을 영웅담의 주인공이에요.
phrases.en: He is the hero of this village's hero stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기 속에서 영웅이 되는 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who is the hero in such a story.

explain_en: Besides stories about heroes, it is used in daily talk for someone boasting about great things they did, as in '영웅담을 늘어놓다'. A similar word is '무용담', which fits stories of brave fights or adventures better.

examples.ko: 윷놀이는 윷가락 네 개를 던져서 해요.
examples.en: You play yutnori by throwing four yut sticks.
I threw the yut sticks and got a mo.
These are yut sticks my grandfather made himself.
One of the yut sticks rolled out of the room.

examples.ko: 설날에 가족이 모여 윷가락 던지는 소리가 방 안에 가득했어요.
examples.en: On Lunar New Year, the sound of the family throwing yut sticks filled the room.

examples.ko: 윷가락이 어디 갔는지 같이 찾아 주세요.
examples.en: Please help me look for where the yut sticks went.

explain: 윷놀이에서 던지는 막대 네 개를 가리켜요. 놀이 이름은 '윷놀이'이고, 설날 같은 명절에 가족끼리 많이 해요.

phrases.example: 설날에 온 가족이 모여서 윷놀이를 했어요.
phrases.en: On New Year's Day the whole family gathered and played yutnori.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윷가락으로 하는 놀이의 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the game played with yutgarak.

phrases.en: We threw the yut sticks in turn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윷가락을 줄여서 '윷'이라고 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: People often shorten yutgarak to just 윷.

phrases.en: The yut sticks fell on the floor and we checked the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 던진 윷가락이 바닥에 놓이는 순간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the moment the thrown sticks land on the floor.

explain_en: It refers to the four sticks you throw in yutnori. The game itself is called '윷놀이', and families often play it on holidays such as Lunar New Year.

en: to criticize; to review; to comment

examples.ko: 그는 영화를 평론하는 일을 십 년째 하고 있어요.
examples.en: He has been reviewing films for ten years.

examples.ko: 신문에 새 소설을 평론한 글이 실렸어요.
examples.en: A piece reviewing the new novel was published in the newspaper.
The experts commented coolly on this game.

examples.ko: 친구들끼리 영화를 평론하면 이야기가 끝이 없어요.
examples.en: When friends critique movies together, the conversation never ends.

examples.ko: 작품을 평론하려면 먼저 끝까지 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To review a work, you first have to read it to the end.

examples.ko: 방송에서 요즘 가요를 평론해 달라는 부탁을 받았어요.
examples.en: I was asked to critique today's pop songs on a broadcast.

explain: 그냥 의견을 말하는 '말하다'와 달리, 영화, 책, 음악, 정치 같은 것을 분석해서 좋고 나쁨을 따지는 것이에요. 그 일을 하는 사람은 '평론가'라고 해요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '평가하다'나 '리뷰하다'도 써요.

phrases.en: The judge evaluates the work strictly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평론하다'보다 가볍고 넓게 써서, 좋고 나쁨이나 가치를 따질 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and broader than 평론하다; used for judging quality or value in general.

phrases.en: The reporter sharply criticized the new movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평론하다'와 비슷하지만 나쁜 점을 짚어 말하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 평론하다, but with a stronger sense of pointing out flaws.

phrases.en: He is a famous film critic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평론하다'를 직업으로 하는 사람을 부르는 말이고, 앞에 분야를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the person who does 평론하다 as a job; put the field in front.

explain_en: Unlike '말하다' (to say), which just states an opinion, this means analyzing something like a film, book, music or politics and weighing its merits. A person who does it is a '평론가' (critic). In casual talk people also say '평가하다' or '리뷰하다'.

t90.ax: He has been reviewing films for ten years.

examples.ko: 누구나 문화생활을 자유롭게 향유할 권리가 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has the right to freely enjoy cultural life.
These days, people enjoy all kinds of content on their smartphones.

examples.ko: 그는 은퇴한 뒤 여유로운 삶을 향유하고 있어요.
examples.en: After retiring, he is enjoying a leisurely life.

examples.ko: 예전에는 일부 사람만 향유하던 문화가 이제 대중화됐어요.
examples.en: A culture once enjoyed only by some people has now become popular.

examples.ko: 도시 사람들도 자연을 향유할 수 있도록 공원을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: They added parks so that city people can also enjoy nature.

examples.ko: 우리 세대는 풍요로운 환경을 향유하며 자랐어요.
examples.en: Our generation grew up enjoying an abundant environment.

explain: '즐기다'나 '누리다'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있고, 문화·자연·권리·혜택처럼 큰 것을 누린다는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '즐기다'나 '누리다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 도시에 살면 다양한 문화를 향유하기 쉬워요.
phrases.en: If you live in a city, it is easy to enjoy a variety of culture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문화, 자연, 권리처럼 큰 것을 누릴 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits big things such as culture, nature, or rights.

phrases.example: 많은 사람이 그 혜택을 향유하지 못해요.
phrases.en: Many people cannot enjoy that benefit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혜택이나 권리를 누리지 못하는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for situations where people cannot enjoy a benefit or right.

phrases.en: We are enjoying freedom to the fullest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '향유하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that sounds more natural in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It is similar to '즐기다' or '누리다', but more formal, with the feel of enjoying something big like culture, nature, rights or benefits. In everyday conversation people usually use '즐기다' or '누리다'.

dis.h: enjoy culture or rights; formal, written
gh: show joy; a person's happy feeling
enjoy an activity, hobby, or time

p.n: 누리다 is more natural in speech; 향유하다 sounds written and formal.

t90.ax: After retiring, he is enjoying a leisurely life.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 백 년 된 고목이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A hundred-year-old tree stands at the entrance to the village.
The grandmothers are resting under the old tree.
The old tree fell in the typhoon and blocked the road.
This old tree turns yellow every autumn.
I want to become a reliable person like an old tree.
A bird built a nest in the old tree.

explain: '고목나무'라고도 하지만 대화에서는 그냥 '고목'이라고 해요. 마을을 지켜 온 오래된 나무처럼 존경하는 느낌으로 많이 쓰고, 힘이 빠진 모습을 비유할 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 마을 앞 고목나무에 새가 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: A bird is perched on the old tree in front of the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고목'과 같은 뜻이지만 글이나 이야기에서 가끔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 고목, occasionally used in writing and stories.

phrases.en: That tree has become an old tree before I knew it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세월이 지나 나무가 아주 오래되었다는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the change of a tree becoming very old over time.

phrases.en: There is a very old tree in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고목'을 일상 대화에서 쉽게 풀어 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 고목.

explain_en: People also say '고목나무', but in conversation plain '고목' is enough. It is often used with a respectful feeling for an old tree that has watched over a village, and sometimes as a metaphor for someone who has lost strength.

examples.ko: 가을이 되자 설악산 굽이굽이에 단풍이 들었어요.
examples.en: When autumn came, every winding fold of Seoraksan was covered in colorful leaves.
The river winds its way along to the sea.
We climbed for a long time along the winding mountain road.
The train runs along the winding railway track.

examples.ko: 굽이굽이 돌아온 길이라 더 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: It's a road we came by after many twists and turns, so it stays in my memory more.

examples.ko: 우리 할머니 인생에는 굽이굽이마다 사연이 있어요.
examples.en: Every twist and turn of my grandmother's life has a story.

explain: 길이나 강, 산줄기가 여러 번 휘어진 모양에 쓰고, '굽이굽이 흐르다', '굽이굽이 돌다'처럼 말해요. '굽이굽이마다 사연이 있다'처럼 힘들고 복잡했던 인생을 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The river winds along its way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강이 여러 번 휘며 흐르는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a river flowing with many bends.

phrases.en: The bus wound its way up the mountain road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 따라 여러 번 방향을 틀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when turning many times along a road.

phrases.en: I walked along the long winding road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이어진'과 함께 길이 계속 휘어 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 이어진, it shows a path that keeps curving on.
phrases.en_equiv: a path winding on and on

explain_en: It describes roads, rivers and mountain ridges that bend many times, as in '굽이굽이 흐르다' (flow winding) or '굽이굽이 돌다'. It can also be used figuratively for a hard, complicated life, as in '굽이굽이마다 사연이 있다'.

t90.ax: The river winds its way along to the sea.

examples.en: I put an orchid pot in the living room.

examples.ko: 난초는 물을 너무 많이 주면 죽어요.
examples.en: An orchid dies if you give it too much water.
The orchid bloomed white and smells lovely.
I gave the teacher an orchid as a gift.
Orchid paintings often appear in East Asian painting.

examples.ko: 이 난초는 일 년에 한 번 꽃이 피어요.
examples.en: This orchid blooms once a year.

explain: 개업이나 승진 축하 선물로 '난 화분'을 많이 보내요. 줄여서 '난'이라고도 해요. 옛 그림에서는 매화·난초·국화·대나무, 즉 '사군자'의 하나예요.

phrases.example: 친구가 개업 선물로 난초 화분을 보냈어요.
phrases.en: My friend sent an orchid pot as an opening gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선물이나 집 안 장식으로 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for gifts and home decoration.

phrases.en: My grandfather grows orchids on the balcony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물을 기를 때 '키우다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 키우다 when raising plants.

phrases.en: The orchid flowers are in full bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물 전체가 아니라 꽃만 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about just the flower, not the whole plant.

explain_en: Orchid pots are a popular gift for a business opening or a promotion. It is shortened to '난'. In old paintings it is one of the '사군자': plum, orchid, chrysanthemum, and bamboo.

en: all things; everything in the world

examples.en: When spring comes, all living things wake up.
There is a saying that humans are the lords of all creation.

examples.ko: 이 시는 만물에 대한 사랑을 노래해요.
examples.en: This poem sings of love for all things.
My grandmother told me to treasure everything in the world.
When winter comes, everything rests quietly.

examples.ko: 사람은 자연 속에서 만물과 함께 살아가요.
examples.en: People live together with all things in nature.

explain: 자연과 우주에 있는 모든 것을 크게 말할 때 써요. '봄이 되면 만물이 깨어난다'처럼 글, 시, 격언 같은 말투에 어울려요. 평소 대화에서는 '모든 것'이나 '세상 모든 것'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 세상 만물은 시간이 지나면 모두 변해요.
phrases.en: All things in the world change as time passes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세상'을 앞에 붙이면 '모든 것'이라는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting 세상 before it makes the meaning of 'everything' clearer.

phrases.en: Humans are called the lords of all creation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 가장 뛰어난 존재라는 뜻으로 쓰는 고정된 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed phrase meaning humans are the most superior beings.

phrases.example: 비가 오고 햇볕이 비치면 만물이 자라요.
phrases.en: When it rains and the sun shines, all things grow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연이 살아나는 모습을 글처럼 크게 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a literary, broad description of nature coming alive.

explain_en: Used to speak broadly of everything in nature and the universe. It fits a written, poetic or proverb-like tone, as in '봄이 되면 만물이 깨어난다'. In ordinary conversation people say '모든 것' or '세상 모든 것'.

en: strongly; richly (of a smell or mood)

examples.ko: 가을 숲에서 낙엽 냄새가 물씬 났어요.
examples.en: The smell of fallen leaves rose strongly in the autumn forest.

examples.ko: 이 식당에 들어서면 옛날 분위기가 물씬 풍겨요.
examples.en: When you walk into this restaurant, an old-time atmosphere comes through strongly.
The smell of doenjang stew is wafting up strongly from the kitchen.
When the rain stopped, the smell of earth spread thickly.

examples.ko: 이 사진에서는 어린 시절의 향수가 물씬 느껴져요.
examples.en: You can strongly feel nostalgia for childhood in this photo.

examples.ko: 이곳은 시골 정취가 물씬 풍기는 마을이에요.
examples.en: This is a village that gives off a strong country charm.

explain: 냄새, 분위기, 느낌이 확 짙게 느껴질 때 써요. '풍기다, 나다, 느껴지다'와 자주 같이 나오고, 단순히 정도만 높이는 '아주'와는 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.example: 이 골목에서는 옛날 분위기가 물씬 풍겨요.
phrases.en: This alley gives off a strong old-time atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분위기나 냄새가 짙게 느껴질 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a strong mood or smell.

phrases.en: A strong smell of bread comes from the kitchen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새가 확 퍼질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a smell spreads strongly.

phrases.example: 그 그림에서 가을 느낌이 물씬 느껴져요.
phrases.en: You can strongly feel autumn in that painting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 느낌이나 분위기가 짙게 전해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a feeling comes across richly.

explain_en: Use it when a smell, mood or feeling comes across thick and strong. It often pairs with '풍기다', '나다' and '느껴지다', and it is not a plain intensifier like '아주'.

examples.ko: 눈이 송이송이 내려서 온 동네가 하얘졌어요.
examples.en: Snow fell in big flakes and the whole town turned white.
Grapes hung in plump bunches in the vineyard.
Cherry blossoms are blooming in clusters on every branch.
I put roses into the vase, one bloom after another.

examples.ko: 국화가 정원에 송이송이 피어서 향기가 좋아요.
examples.en: Chrysanthemums are blooming in clusters in the garden and smell lovely.

examples.ko: 하얀 목화가 송이송이 열린 밭을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a field where white cotton bolls grew in clusters.

explain: '송이'는 꽃, 포도, 눈송이를 세는 말이라서 '송이송이'는 그런 것이 여럿 모여 피거나 내리는 모습을 그려요. 주로 꽃이 피거나 눈이 올 때 쓰고, 시나 노래 가사처럼 느낌을 살리는 글에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: When spring came, flowers bloomed in clusters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 여럿 피는 모습에 가장 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits best with many flowers blooming.

phrases.en: Big snowflakes are falling one after another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 탐스럽게 내릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when snow falls in big, lovely flakes.

phrases.en: The grapes hung in bunches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포도처럼 송이로 열리는 열매에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for fruit that grows in bunches like grapes.

explain_en: '송이' is a counter for flowers, grapes and snowflakes, so '송이송이' paints a picture of many of them gathered, blooming or falling. It is used for blooming flowers or falling snow and suits poems or song lyrics that want to create a feeling.

t90.ax: Grapes hung in plump bunches in the vineyard.

en: to take a lesson; to model

examples.ko: 이번 실수를 거울삼아 다음에는 더 조심할게요.
examples.en: I'll learn from this mistake and be more careful next time.
Take your senior's experience as a lesson.
People who learn from failure end up succeeding.
You should learn from the past and prepare for the future.

examples.ko: 회사는 그 사고를 거울삼아서 안전 규칙을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The company took that accident as a lesson and changed its safety rules.

examples.ko: 남의 잘못도 거울삼으면 많이 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you learn even from others' mistakes, you can gain a lot.

explain: '~을/를 거울삼아'의 꼴로 가장 많이 쓰고, 지난 일이나 남의 일에서 교훈을 얻는다는 뜻이에요. '교훈으로 삼다'와 비슷하지만 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Taking the past as a lesson, let's move forward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어가 가장 많이 쓰이는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form of the headword.

phrases.en: I took my older brother's mistake as a lesson.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 교훈을 얻었다고 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense, for when a lesson has already been drawn.

phrases.en: I'll take this failure as a lesson.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 쉽고 말하는 느낌이 나는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, more conversational way to say it.

explain_en: It is most often used in the form '~을/를 거울삼아', meaning to draw a lesson from past events or others' experiences. It is close to '교훈으로 삼다' but sounds a bit more written.

en: to make a firm decision; to decide resolutely

examples.en: The boss made a firm decision and chose to move the factory.
Now is really the time to make up your mind.

examples.ko: 그는 오랜 고민 끝에 회사를 떠나기로 결단했어요.
examples.en: After long deliberation, he resolved to leave the company.

examples.ko: 어려운 순간에는 빨리 결단하는 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: In hard moments, you need someone who decides quickly.
Mom resolved to move to a bigger hospital.
I did not have the courage to decide, so I kept putting it off.

explain: 오래 망설이다가 마음을 굳게 정하는 큰 결정이에요. 점심 메뉴를 정할 때는 '결정하다'를 쓰고, 직장을 그만두거나 이사를 가는 것처럼 용기가 필요한 선택에 결단하다를 써요. '결단을 내리다'라는 말도 자주 해요.

phrases.en: After long thought, I made a firm decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결단하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 자주 들리는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 결단하다 and more common in speech.

phrases.en: Leaving the company was a big decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결단'을 명사로 써서 용기가 필요한 선택을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 결단 as a noun for a choice that takes courage.

phrases.en: Our team leader is decisive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨리 마음을 정하는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a person who decides firmly.

explain_en: It is a big decision made firmly after hesitating for a long time. For choosing a lunch menu you use '결정하다', and 결단하다 fits choices that need courage, like quitting a job or moving. '결단을 내리다' is also a common phrase.

gh: everyday word for choosing or fixing something
decide a case as a judge
settle for good; make final and confirmed

p.n: 결단하다 stresses a firm, brave decision; 결정하다 is neutral.

examples.en: The child fell and wailed.
Everyone sobbed loudly at the end of the movie.

examples.ko: 친구가 이별 얘기를 하며 꺼이꺼이 울더라고요.
examples.en: My friend bawled while talking about the breakup.

examples.ko: 그는 합격 소식에 꺼이꺼이 소리 내어 울었어요.
examples.en: He cried out loud, sobbing, at the news that he passed.
I could hear loud sobbing from the next room.

examples.ko: 꺼이꺼이 울고 나니까 마음이 좀 가벼워졌어요.
examples.en: After sobbing my heart out, I felt a bit lighter.

explain: 거의 '울다'와 함께 쓰고, 목이 메어 숨을 끊어 가며 크게 우는 소리를 나타내요. '엉엉'은 소리 내어 크게 우는 모양이고, '꺼이꺼이'는 목이 메어 울음이 끊기는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 이별 소식을 듣고 친구가 꺼이꺼이 울었어요.
phrases.en: My friend heard about the breakup and sobbed loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 부사와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 목이 메어 크게 우는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for this adverb. It describes crying loudly with a choked voice.

phrases.example: 졸업식에서 선생님을 보자 꺼이꺼이 울음을 터뜨렸어요.
phrases.en: I burst into loud sobs when I saw my teacher at the graduation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참고 있던 울음이 갑자기 터져 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when held-back tears suddenly burst out.

phrases.en: The child lost a toy and cried loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 '엉엉'은 소리 내어 크게 우는 모양이고, '꺼이꺼이'는 울음이 끊기는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but '엉엉' is loud wailing, while '꺼이꺼이' has more of a choked, broken sound.

explain_en: It is used almost only with '울다' and describes crying hard with a choked voice, breaking for breath. '엉엉' is loud crying in general, while '꺼이꺼이' stresses the choked, broken sound.

examples.ko: 이번 시험에 떨어지고 나서 다시금 마음을 다잡았어요.
examples.en: After failing this exam, I pulled myself together once more.
I will steady my scattered mind and start studying.
You have to keep your focus to avoid mistakes.
I take a walk every morning to steady my mind.
Since it is a new year, I decided to renew my resolve.
The team leader pulled the wavering team back together.

explain: '마음을 다잡다'가 가장 흔한 쓰임이고, 정신, 자세, 분위기 같은 말과도 같이 써요. 흐트러진 것을 다시 단단히 바로잡는 느낌이라, 그냥 '잡다'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I failed, but I steadied my mind and started again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 쓰임으로, 흔들린 마음을 바로잡는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, meaning to regain composure after wavering.

phrases.en: I felt sleepy, so I pulled myself together and studied.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집중이 흐트러졌을 때 다시 정신을 차린다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of regaining focus when concentration slips.

phrases.en: I straightened up my posture before the interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸가짐이나 태도를 다시 단정히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when tidying up one's bearing or attitude again.

explain_en: The most common use is '마음을 다잡다', and it also goes with words like spirit, posture and atmosphere. It feels like firmly re-steadying something that had loosened, which differs from plain '잡다'.

t90.ax: You have to keep your focus to avoid mistakes.
